reproduction_target: Computational phylogenetic characterization of a novel triple-reassortant H5N1: maximum-likelihood phylogenies inferred independently for each of the eight IAV genome segments (plus a large ML tree of 11,820 Americas NP sequences) to determine the lineage constellation of the H5N1-Arg_Feb2025 viruses. NGS genome assembly/consensus is upstream but delegated to a previously published protocol (ref 6) with no detail in this prose.
granularity_note: This is a short bioRxiv brief report with NO dedicated Methods/Materials section, NO Code availability statement, and NO named bioinformatics software (no tool names, no versions, no substitution model, no alignment tool, no bootstrap settings). Computational analysis is described only narratively ('phylogenies were inferred independently for each of the eight gene segments'; 'Maximum likelihood trees'; 'Phylogenetic tree inferred using ML methods for 11,820 NP sequences'). Sequencing is 'according to previously described protocols (6)'. Two coarse C-layer steps are recorded (assembly/consensus; ML phylogenetics). Wet-lab RRT-PCR subtyping and NGS library prep/sequencing counted in W (layer W / OOS for computational reproduction), not verdicted. No tool named anywhere in the text, so no per-tool step decomposition is possible; steps are at the operation level.
